hypothesis: An adversary who compromised Windows hosts in this network stole credentials from them (MITRE ATT&CK tactic: Credential Access).

frame.restated: An adversary with access to Windows hosts on this network stole credentials from those hosts.
frame.what_would_confirm: Observable evidence such as LSASS process access or memory dumps, suspicious use of credential-dumping tools (e.g., Mimikatz, ProcDump, comsvcs.dll), access to SAM/SECURITY/SYSTEM registry hives or NTDS.dit, Kerberoasting or AS-REP roasting attempts, or anomalous authentication using stolen credentials from compromised Windows hosts.
frame.what_would_refute: Observable absence of credential theft indicators on the compromised Windows hosts, including no LSASS access or memory dumping, no credential-dump tool execution, no unauthorized access to credential stores or registry hives, and no authentication or privilege escalation activity attributable to stolen credentials.

verdict.rationale: The credential-access hypothesis is confirmed by F01: on scranton.dmevals.local, a hidden PowerShell process launched by control.exe from a steganographic payload in monkey.png accessed lsass.exe with full-access masks 0x1f3fff and 0x1fffff and injected an unbacked remote thread into LSASS (Sysmon EID 10 and EID 8, StartModule '-'), which is a high-confidence T1003.001 LSASS credential dumping pattern. Independent Security EID 4656 corroborates the same handle requests. The same activity chain also compiled C# in memory, wrote a .pfx, and then used PsExec64 with the cleartext password of DMEVALS\pbeesly against NASHUA, further supporting credential theft and reuse. F02-F04 are benign/not-evidenced for Get-Process -IncludeUserName, SAM hive dumping, and Kerberoasting, but they do not refute the confirmed LSASS credential dumping. Thus the hypothesis that an adversary stole credentials from compromised Windows hosts is confirmed.

checks.purpose: Stack every process-access event whose target is LSASS by the accessing image; rare/unsigned images touching lsass.exe are the primary credential-dumping signal.
Surface rare access masks on LSASS (e.g. 0x1010 / 0x1410 / 0x143a / 0x1fffff) which indicate read-memory/handle-duplication instead of benign query access.

args.query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon-default METADATA _id, _index | WHERE event.code == "10" AND TO_LOWER(win.TargetImage) LIKE "*lsass*" | KEEP @timestamp, host.name, win.SourceImage, win.TargetImage, win.GrantedAccess, win.CallTrace, _id, _index

checks.purpose: Read the individual LSASS-access events (host, source image, granted access, call trace) for any suspicious entry returned by the aggregations.

findings.title: LSASS memory accessed with full-access masks and an unbacked remote thread injected by PowerShell on scranton
findings.summary: On 2020-05-02 03:05:16 UTC on scranton.dmevals.local, C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe (PID 2976, user DMEVALS\pbeesly) opened C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe (PID 736) with GrantedAccess 0x1f3fff and 0x1fffff (Sysmon EID 10) and created a remote thread in it (Sysmon EID 8, NewThreadId 912) starting at 0x00000117610E0000 with StartModule '-' (code in unbacked memory). Security EID 4656 independently shows the same PowerShell process (SubjectUserName pbeesly) requesting handles to \Device\HarddiskVolume2\Windows\System32\lsass.exe with AccessMask 0x1f3fff and 0x1fffff at 23:05:16 local (=03:05:16Z). That PowerShell process was launched at 02:58:44 by C:\Windows\System32\control.exe with a hidden command line that decodes an ASCII payload from C:\Users\pbeesly\Downloads\monkey.png (steganography) and IEXes it, and it then compiled C# in memory via csc.exe (Temp\RES2758.tmp) and wrote a .pfx to Downloads. A second in-memory loader (reflective delegate via UnsafeNativeMethods.GetProcAddress plus a base64 shellcode blob) was logged for the same host/user at 03:21:29 after the 03:18:30 restart initiated by pbeesly. This is LSASS memory access/credential dumping (T1003.001) on scranton by the pbeesly session; the same account then used PsExec64 with the cleartext password of dmevals\pbeesly against \\NASHUA (PSEXESVC installed 4x on nashua, python.exe run from C:\Windows\Temp).

findings.title: wsmprovhost.exe full-access handle to LSASS on nashua is Get-Process -IncludeUserName enumeration (benign)
findings.summary: On 2020-05-02 03:09:29 UTC on nashua.dmevals.local, C:\windows\system32\wsmprovhost.exe (PID 7720, pbeesly PS-remoting session) accessed C:\windows\system32\lsass.exe with GrantedAccess 0x1f3fff. The same 0x1f3fff mask was requested against a long list of unrelated processes (ApplicationFrameHost.exe, browser_broker.exe, conhost.exe, ctfmon.exe, DllHost.exe, dwm.exe, Explorer.EXE, fontdrvhost.exe, LogonUI.exe), and the PS remoting script block recorded at 03:09:28 on nashua is 'Get-Process -IncludeUserName | Select-Object UserName,SessionId | ...' - the standard signature of Get-Process -IncludeUserName enumerating process owners, not targeted LSASS reading. No dump write or remote thread into lsass exists for this host (Sysmon EID 8 query for nashua returned nothing).

findings.title: Only lsass.exe itself wrote to the SAM hive; no SAM dump or hive copy observed
findings.summary: Registry-write telemetry matching *SAM* on 2020-05-02 contains only two events, both on scranton.dmevals.local: lsass.exe setting HKLM\SAM\SAM\Domains\Account\F at 03:19:10 (immediately after the 03:18:30 restart initiated by pbeesly) and LogonUI.exe setting the LogonUI\SessionData\2\LoggedOnSAMUser value at 03:20:46 - i.e. legitimate post-logon SAM bookkeeping by the SAM owner process. No hive extraction tooling was observed: Security 4688 has no reg.exe/reg save, esentutl, ntdsutil or vssadmin executions, and no file-create event writes the SAM/SECURITY/SYSTEM hive files. SAM-hash theft is therefore not demonstrated in this window (LSASS itself was attacked instead - see the T1003.001 finding).

findings.title: Kerberos ticketing is AES256-only service/TGT traffic - no RC4 Kerberoasting pattern
findings.summary: In windows.security the 28 Kerberos service-ticket requests (EID 4769) are all TicketEncryptionType 0x12 (AES256) for user pbeesly@DMEVALS.LOCAL against machine accounts (ServiceName NEWYORK$, NASHUA$, krbtgt) with Status 0x0, and the 14 TGT requests (EID 4768) are likewise 0x12 for pbeesly/krbtgt - no RC4 (0x17/0x18) ticket storm and no anomalous service SPNs, so Kerberoasting is not evidenced. In the separate, non-overlapping zeek capture window (2020-04-30) every Kerberos record carries cipher aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96 and the only failures are AS-REQ exchanges answered with KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED for pbeesly (normal pre-authentication, which also argues against AS-REP roasting of that account).
